title: Lina's Warm Buns
markdown:
The kitchen smelled warm and sweet. Lina put her hot cross buns on the windowsill, for the village fair. Moss the hedgehog watched, nose twitching.

“They look wonderful, Lina,” Auntie June said. “So lovely and warm.”

Lina sighed and touched a bun. The cozy warmth was fading. Moss nudged one. “They’re not as warm,” he whispered. A problem for the fair.

Lina frowned. The air above the buns shimmered a little. Warmth floating away, like a gentle river leaving.

“Let’s try something.” A soft tea towel. “If the warm is drifting away, we can wrap it like a cozy blanket.” She draped the towel over the buns.

They waited. Moss nudged a bun under the towel. “It’s still warm!”

For comparison, Lina set two buns on a wire rack in the open air. Those cooled faster. The towel-wrapped ones kept their hug.

“Look!” She clapped. “The warmth stays longer when we help it stay.”

Auntie June beamed. “Heat likes to move from where there’s lots of it to where there’s less. Wrapping them keeps them snug. The rack lets the air take the heat away.”

With the buns wrapped warmly, Lina, Moss, and Auntie June walked to the fair. Villagers loved them. “Wonderfully warm!” said Mrs. Gable.

They sold the last bun. Lina looked at Moss. She did not ask what other journeys heat takes. The towel, folded in the basket, still smelled of spice, which is a kind of leftover warmth, and enough.
characters: Lina (patient inventor), Moss (hedgehog), Auntie June (aunt), Mrs. Gable (villager)
